OBSERVED ACROSS ONE FULL SESSION, 2026-08-17, and recorded because the instances are already in the graph separately and the PATTERN is not. FOUR TIMES IN ONE DAY, THE FAILURE WAS THE SAME: A FACT WAS ASSERTED WHERE IT COULD HAVE BEEN COUNTED. Measurement caught it every time, and in three of the four the assertion had already been acted on.

(1) RELAYED A FALSE CLAIM FROM AN INSTRUMENT. `loop_status` said an answered question had never reached the design; it had been there, accepted and approver-signed, since 2026-08-11. Told to the user as fact before the graph was checked. Cost: a wrong opening summary. → `fact:defect-loop-status-asserts-an-answer-never-reached-the-design-from-a-fact-that-cannot-say-so`

(2) DECIDED AGAINST A FIX ON AN UNMEASURED COST. Declined to rename `disconnected_community` because it would "break every consumer". Measured afterwards: 14 code files, 6 docs, PERSISTED AS DATA NOWHERE — no migration existed to protect against. Cost: shipped a half-fix that had to be reversed hours later. → `dec:a-misnaming-is-fixed-in-the-message-not-the-key`

(3) WROTE AN UNCHECKED CLAIM ABOUT A CHECK. A doc comment said the compiler enforced that `HealCategory::ALL` lists every variant. It does not. Caught before commit by re-reading rather than by anything mechanical. Cost: none, and only because it was noticed. → `cap:a-sweep-names-its-own-scope-and-the-category-names-what-it-computes`

(4) ALMOST PROPOSED A DETECTOR ON PLAUSIBILITY. Oscillation detection looked obviously buildable. Counting first showed only 23 of 187 artifacts carry any checksum history and 3 have more than one prior value, because `design_holds` accepts do not snapshot. The detector would have reported zero forever and been believed. Cost: none — the measurement happened before the proposal. → `dec:idea-an-artifact-whose-checksum-returns-is-an-agent-going-in-circles`

⭐ THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING, and it is why this is worth a node rather than an apology. An asserted cost that STOPS work is nearly invisible when it is wrong, because nothing happens and there is no failure to notice — instance (2) would have stood indefinitely if the user had not stated a rule that forced the question. An asserted claim that DRIVES work usually gets caught by the work failing. So the dangerous direction is the one that argues for inaction, and it is the direction with no natural feedback.

⇒ WHY IT BELONGS BESIDE THIS RULE: `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` already carries "MEASURE THE COST BEFORE LETTING IT DECIDE" as a clause, derived from instance (2) alone. Three further instances in the same day say that clause is the load-bearing half of the rule rather than an aside, and that it generalises past cost to any claim an agent uses to close a question.

📌 AND IT IS DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO THE AGENT-PITFALL WORK opened the same day (`dec:idea-which-agent-pitfalls-can-reflow2-actually-reach`). None of the four is on the user's pitfall list, and they are not code-writing failures — they are DESIGN-REASONING failures, committed while using the design brain. That may be a class the list does not cover.

⚠️ ONE LOOSE END FROM THE SAME SESSION THAT WAS NOT RESOLVED, recorded here because it is the one thing that could NOT be measured and therefore stayed open. `reflow2_check.py` printed "FAILED — 1 finding" once, immediately after an export that carried a `sync_note` about the file having moved, and then returned OK on four consecutive runs against the committed file with both CI jobs green. The failing finding was never captured — it was chained behind a `;` with a push and scrolled past. LOW CONFIDENCE, NOT REPRODUCED, and possibly a transient of the export's own sync bookkeeping rather than a real drift. Recorded so a later session meeting the same thing knows it has been seen once and never explained.
